title: Microsoft Teams: invite people to register for events by email
summary: The briefing accurately reports the rollout, registration eligibility and custom-domain restriction in Microsoft's notice. The admin paths and PowerShell calls are supported; one minor clarification should acknowledge that the cmdlet reference still labels Events policy as preview.

claims.claim: Organisers can send email invitations containing a registration link for Teams events with registration enabled.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams is expanding the Invite to register experience for Teams events with registration enabled. Organizers can select people to receive an email invitation with a link to register for the event.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The sending-domain control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Send email notifications from your domain > Use a custom send-from domain address.
claims.quote: select Settings. ... Select Org settings. ... select Organization profile. ... select Send email notifications from your domain. ... select Use a custom send-from domain address.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation for the Microsoft 365 notification sending-domain setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Send email notifications from your domain" PowerShell Microsoft Graph API; "Send email notifications from your domain" "Set" "Graph". Opened the Select the domain to use for email page; results document UI configuration, not an operation for this setting.

claims.claim: The sending-domain setting is opt-in.
claims.quote: This setting is an opt-in setting that allows the Microsoft 365 system administrators to select a verified domain within the tenant.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The sending-domain setting can take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: The setting can take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: Only domains registered within the tenant can be used for the notification sending-domain setting.
claims.quote: Only domains registered within your tenant can be used.

claims.claim: Domain ownership must be verified.
claims.quote: Domain ownership must be verified through the existing add domains process within Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Microsoft Teams supports the Microsoft 365 notification sending-domain setting.
claims.quote: The following products currently support this feature: ... Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: Configuring the sending domain makes event notification emails use the chosen verified custom domain.
claims.quote: admins can configure Teams events email notifications to be sent from a verified custom domain instead of Microsoft default addresses.

claims.claim: Without a custom domain, event emails use Microsoft-provided addresses.
claims.quote: While events can function without a custom domain, emails are sent from Microsoft-provided addresses that might be less recognizable to recipients.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends a custom domain for event emails to improve deliverability.
claims.quote: Set up a custom domain for event emails (recommended) ... Increase email deliverability and reduce spam classification.

claims.claim: Microsoft says using a custom domain reduces spam classification of event emails.
claims.quote: Increase email deliverability and reduce spam classification.

claims.claim: Microsoft says a custom domain builds greater trust for external audiences receiving invitations.
claims.quote: Build greater trust for external audiences receiving invitations and updates.

claims.claim: The smaller-event attendee-access setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events up to 1k attendees.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... in the Who can attend events up to 1k attendees dropdown list, select one of the following

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EventAccessType EveryoneInCompanyExcludingGuests restricts smaller-event attendance to users in the organisation.
claims.quote: To only allow users in your organization to attend events with up to 1,000 attendees created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EventAccessType EveryoneInCompanyExcludingGuests
claims.fix: Add to Governance controls: 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference still labels Events policy as preview, although the admin guidance documents these settings without that label.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/teams/set-csteamseventspolicy, which states 'Note that this policy is currently still in preview.' The printed calls need no change.

claims.claim: The large-audience attendee-access setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests restricts large-audience events to the organisation and guests.
claims.quote: To only allow users in your organization and guests to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests

claims.claim: The smaller-event attendee-access setting defaults to Everyone.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone.

claims.claim: The large-audience attendee-access setting defaults to Everyone.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone.

claims.claim: No dedicated Invite to register on/off setting is documented in the admin UI or automation at the time of writing in November 2026.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe Invite to register itself beyond the supplied roadmap and notice.

claims.claim: In the Events app, organisers choose whether to turn registration on while scheduling the event.

claims.claim: In the Events app, the registration setting cannot be changed after the event is first saved.
claims.quote: After you save your event, you won't be able to change this setting. ... To modify registration, registration must have been turned on before you first saved the event while scheduling it.
